Chapter 8: Deepening the Conversation—Asking Better Questions
As we start to recognize and receive revelation more naturally, something interesting happens. Our spiritual conversations begin to shift. Instead of just looking for quick answers to whatever challenge pops up, we start asking deeper, more open-ended questions. These are the kinds of questions that open the door to real growth, greater understanding, and even transformation.
You’ve probably noticed this in your own life. The questions you bring to God—well, they really shape the answers you get back. If you stick to simple yes-or-no questions, the guidance you receive is usually clear, but it’s also a bit limited. But when you try something like, “What would you have me learn from this?” or “How can I serve today?”, suddenly you’re inviting a deeper, broader kind of insight. It’s a little like opening a window and letting in more light.
Think of it this way: it’s moving from a transactional relationship—just asking for quick fixes—to something more like a partnership. Instead of seeing God as a problem-solver, you start seeking His wisdom, His perspective, and His companionship in every part of your life.
So, how do you actually deepen the conversation? Here are a few practical ideas:
First, try asking open-ended questions. Instead of focusing only on your immediate needs, invite guidance that stretches you, that helps you see the bigger picture.
Next, listen for themes. Sometimes, you’ll notice recurring impressions or patterns—these might be gentle nudges pointing toward the deeper lessons you’re meant to learn.
Take some time to reflect on your past experiences, too. Look back and see how previous guidance has shaped your journey. What does that suggest about where you’re headed next?
Don’t forget to express gratitude. Even if the insights seem small, take a moment to thank God for them. Gratitude keeps your heart open and receptive.
And finally, invite correction. That takes humility, but it’s powerful. Ask God to show you your blind spots or areas where you could grow.
Picture it like a mentor and apprentice. The apprentice who asks thoughtful, reflective questions doesn’t just get instructions—they receive wisdom and perspective. Over time, the relationship deepens, and the apprentice starts to really understand the mentor’s way of thinking.
You’ll see this play out in everyday life. Maybe you’re facing a tough relationship. Instead of just asking, “How can I fix this?” you might wonder, “What am I being invited to learn about love and patience?” Or, if you’re struggling with a career decision, what if you asked, “How can I use my gifts to serve others?” instead of simply wanting a yes or no?
Here’s the key takeaway: deepening the conversation really transforms your experience of revelation. It’s no longer just about solving problems—it’s about growing in wisdom, compassion, and true partnership with God. The dialogue becomes ongoing, and you’re not just waiting for guidance—you’re actively seeking it, pondering it, and weaving it into your everyday life.
